subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw accept this opt-in public timeout and generic queue-hook contract, including releasing the maintenance lane while a non-cooperative plugin `maintain()` call may continue with only runtime-owned side effects fenced?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and well-proven, but review cannot choose the permanent core/plugin cancellation and configuration contract; repository policy reserves new config and compatibility-sensitive lifecycle behavior for owner judgment.

options.title: Approve opt-in abandonment contract
options.body: Merge the disabled-by-default timeout, runtime-owned fences, persistence checkpoint, and documentation as the supported recovery contract.

options.title: Require cooperative cancellation
options.body: Pause this PR and first define an abort contract on the context-engine maintenance seam so timed-out workers can be stopped rather than abandoned.

options.title: Reuse existing timeout policy
options.body: Replace the new setting with an owner-approved existing compaction or session timeout only if maintainers declare its semantics compatible.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in abandonment contract
recommendation.body: Merge the disabled-by-default timeout, runtime-owned fences, persistence checkpoint, and documentation as the supported recovery contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the documented compaction and context-engine owner for the lifecycle and plugin boundary being changed.
